critical_steps: The source defines Kf as the sum of omega_i squared times theta_i f.
The fusion synthesis operator applies one factor omega_i to each component.
Therefore the synthesis-equation solution has components omega_i theta_i f.
For one weight equal to two, X_w=I/2 and theta=I/4, contradicting the theorem's unweighted norm inequality.
The corrected weighted inequalities follow from minimum norm and orthogonality to the synthesis kernel.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact one-dimensional counterexample together with the Douglas reduced-solution orthogonal decomposition.
integrity.unproved_limits: No complete corrected formula for every downstream consequence is asserted.

scientific_limitations: The finding concerns the weight normalization in Theorem 4.3 and the directly derived pseudoinverse formula in Corollary 4.4.
The weighted minimum-norm inequalities are proved; no complete replacement is claimed for every downstream statement depending on Theorem 4.3.
An unindexed erratum, thesis remark, or informal correction may contain the same observation.
title: Weight normalization breaks a minimum-norm \(K\)-fusion resolution theorem
